title: Gaming & VR Privacy Hardening Checklist
metaDescription: Protect your privacy while gaming and using VR. Complete checklist to secure your data from tracking and collection by gaming platforms.
intro: Gaming platforms and VR headsets collect vast amounts of personal data including gameplay habits, biometric data, voice recordings, and social interactions. This checklist helps you minimize data collection and protect your privacy while gaming.

items.task: Disable data sharing with third parties
items.why: Gaming platforms often share your data with advertisers and analytics companies for targeted marketing and user profiling.
items.howTo: Go to privacy settings in Steam, Epic Games, PlayStation, Xbox, or Nintendo accounts. Turn off data sharing, marketing communications, and third-party integrations. Opt out of analytics programs.

items.why: Public profiles expose your gaming habits, friends list, and activity patterns to strangers and data collectors.
items.howTo: Change profile visibility to private or friends-only. Hide game library, playtime statistics, achievements, and activity feeds from public view in platform settings.

items.task: Turn off voice chat recording and processing
items.why: Gaming platforms may record and analyze voice communications for content moderation and data collection purposes.
items.howTo: Disable voice data collection in platform settings. Turn off voice-to-text features and automatic transcription. Use push-to-talk instead of open microphone.

items.task: Remove unnecessary connected apps and services
items.why: Third-party apps connected to gaming accounts can access your personal data, friends list, and gaming statistics.
items.howTo: Review connected applications in account settings. Remove unused Discord bots, streaming apps, and stat-tracking services. Revoke permissions for unnecessary integrations.

items.why: VR headsets collect sensitive biometric data including eye tracking, facial expressions, and movement patterns that can identify you uniquely.
items.howTo: Disable eye tracking, facial tracking, and gesture recognition in VR settings. Turn off biometric authentication features. Limit sensor data collection to essential functions only.

items.task: Limit room scanning and environment mapping
items.why: VR systems create detailed 3D maps of your living space, potentially exposing personal information about your home and lifestyle.
items.howTo: Use minimal room setup instead of full room scanning. Delete stored room layouts regularly. Turn off automatic environment detection and mapping features.

items.task: Disable VR social features and presence sharing
items.why: VR social features can expose your real-world schedule, location patterns, and personal interactions to other users and platforms.
items.howTo: Turn off online status indicators, presence sharing, and automatic friend suggestions. Disable location-based features and social media integrations in VR settings.

items.why: VR platforms may automatically capture and upload your gameplay, potentially including private moments or personal spaces visible in your environment.
items.howTo: Disable automatic recording and screenshot features. Turn off cloud uploads of captured content. Review and delete stored recordings regularly from device and cloud storage.

items.task: Use Incognito Browser for gaming-related web browsing
items.why: Gaming websites and forums track your browsing habits to build detailed profiles for targeted advertising and data selling.
items.howTo: Download Incognito Browser for gaming-related searches, purchases, and forum browsing. This prevents cross-site tracking and protects your gaming interests from being profiled.

items.task: Use VPN for online gaming when appropriate
items.why: Your ISP and gaming servers can track your location, gaming schedule, and correlate your gaming activity with other online behaviors.
items.howTo: Use a gaming-friendly VPN with low latency servers. Choose servers in your region to minimize ping. Be aware some games block VPN usage in their terms of service.

items.task: Create dedicated email for gaming accounts
items.why: Using your main email for gaming exposes you to data breaches and allows correlation of your gaming activity with other online accounts.
items.howTo: Create a separate email address specifically for gaming accounts. Use an alias or privacy-focused email service. Don't link this email to social media or other personal accounts.

items.task: Enable two-factor authentication on all gaming accounts
items.why: Gaming accounts contain payment information and personal data that are valuable targets for hackers and identity thieves.
items.howTo: Enable 2FA using authenticator apps rather than SMS. Use hardware security keys when available. Set up backup recovery codes and store them securely offline.

items.task: Request data deletion and review retention policies
items.why: Gaming companies store years of detailed behavioral data that can be used to profile you even after you stop using their services.
items.howTo: Submit data deletion requests for unused gaming accounts. Review privacy policies for data retention periods. Request copies of your data to understand what information is collected.

items.task: Remove stored payment methods and use temporary cards
items.why: Stored payment information creates additional privacy risks and enables impulse purchases that gaming companies encourage through psychological manipulation.
items.howTo: Remove saved credit cards from gaming platforms. Use virtual credit card numbers or prepaid cards for gaming purchases. Enable purchase confirmation requirements and spending limits.
